legend: Dysgenetic testis from a 4-year-old girl with a disorder of sex development and 45,X/46,XY mosaicism in which a gonadoblastoma is starting to develop. Note the dysplastic testicular cords/tubules and an early focus of gonadoblastoma in the centre left.

Dysgenetic testis from a 4-year-old girl with a disorder of sex development and 45,X/46,XY mosaicism in which a gonadoblastoma is starting to develop. Closer view of the developing gonadoblastoma in the same case as is shown in Fig. <<#20225>>. Note the basement membrane hyaline deposits and nests of two cellular populations (germ cells and sex cord cells).
Germ cells of gonadoblastoma showing nuclei positive for OCT3/4.
Germ cells of gonadoblastoma showing membranous staining of PLAP.
Sex cord cells of gonadoblastoma showing positive staining of inhibin.
Sex cord cells of gonadoblastoma showing positive nuclear staining of SOX9.

Gonadoblastoma nest with germ cells of variable appearance, from spermatogonia-like cells to cells resembling those of germ cell neoplasia in situ / seminoma / dysgerminoma, as well as incompletely differentiated sex cord cells and round hyaline material. The surrounding spindle cell gonadal stroma contains Leydig-like or lutein-like cells.
source: Figure used in the Gonadoblastoma section of the WHO volume on Classification of Paediatric Tumours, in preparation. Author: Pilar González-Peramato.

legend: Low-power view. A gonadoblastoma in a streak gonad shows the characteristic small nests in a cellular stroma. This case shows extensive calcifications, some with a mulberry-like configuration.
source: Figure used in the Gonadoblastoma section of the WHO volume on Classification of Paediatric Tumours, in preparation. Author: Thomas M. Ulbright.

legend: High-power view. The three components can be seen: germ cells, most resembling those of germ cell neoplasia in situ; sex cord cells; and round deposits of basement membrane matrix. A dissecting pattern is at the top, mimicking a focus of invasive germinoma.
source: Figure used in the Gonadoblastoma section of the WHO volume on Classification of Paediatric Tumours, in preparation. Author: Thomas M. Ulbright.
